jobs.title: The microfilm
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; THE LIBRARIAN — seen mostly as a cardigan at the edge of the panel: a woman of sixty with gray hair in a short bob and half-moon glasses, when the strip lets her face in. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: The college library has the county paper on microfilm back to 1962. Wood looks up the mill's closing. He finds the ad for the derby instead, 1985. Same crab. Nobody drew it; it was a stamp. Panel 1: a young man at a microfilm reader in a library, the reel spinning, a cardigan-clad librarian's shoulder at the frame's edge, black and white, no words (in this panel: WOOD, THE LIBRARIAN). Librarian says "Nineteen ninety-four is the third drawer.". Panel 2: close on a microfilm screen showing an old newspaper classified ad with a small crab printed from a rubber stamp, black and white, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a young man's face lit by a microfilm reader's glow, unimpressed, black and white, no words. Wood says "Fifteen years of this crab and nobody drew it. It's a stamp.". Panel 4: a young man cranking a microfilm reader as the screen blurs between pages, library lights going off in the far stacks, black and white, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @dw_2001_10_09_lot_c is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @cedar_cast is the model sheet for THE LOGGER: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @dw_2001_10_09_lot_c for a finished strip in this style; @cedar_cast for the character CEDAR: the logger at a tailgate, certain about the slash pile / CEDAR: the woman at the chained mill gate who remembers the year she was a cedar; drawn in cutaway with rings inside her, one ring notched.
